plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In this format, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: bidding higher than value risks overpaying relative to my value if I win against a bid between my value and my bid, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily. Since my value is $40, I should bid exactly $40 to maximize expected profit, ensuring I win whenever profitable and never overpay beyond my valuation.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it never costs more than the item is worth, and ensures I win whenever profitable. Bidding above my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against another high bidder. Bidding below risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $13.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if others bid between my value and my bid. Bidding exactly my value ensures I only win when profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. With no prior history to inform deviation, I'll bid my true value of $17.
